title: Benchmark case
description: One graded incident. Each case is derived from a real production failure, stripped of service names, personal names and internal identifiers, then replanted on synthetic metadata. The answer key is what makes this a benchmark rather than a demo.

symptom.description: Exactly what a human would report. Must NOT hint at the cause. `Signups from channel C fell to zero on the 14th` is fair; `the collector for channel C died` gives the answer away.

seed.description: Deterministic instructions for planting this failure into the synthetic warehouse and DataHub instance. Re-running the seed must reproduce the case byte-for-byte, otherwise scores are not comparable across runs.

must_cite.description: Source refs a correct investigation cannot avoid touching. Drives citation recall. Reaching the right verdict without these is scored as a lucky guess and reported separately.

must_not_conclude.description: Root cause keys that look plausible but are wrong here. Concluding one of these counts as a confident-wrong answer, which is scored worse than `inconclusive`.

distractors.description: Real but irrelevant anomalies planted alongside the true cause, so that a correct verdict requires discrimination rather than pattern matching.

provenance.description: Internal only. Never published in the public repository.
